title: Local infinite-residue-field basis reduction for affine groupoids
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $A\ne0$, and let $s,t,e,i,c$ make them an absolute groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Set $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp$ and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. Assume the homomorphism $\phi:A\otimes_C A\to B$, $a\otimes a'\mapsto\sigma(a)\tau(a')$, is surjective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $C$ there exists a flat local homomorphism $C_{\mathfrak p}\to D$ of nonzero local rings, with infinite residue field; every such homomorphism is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Here $C_{\mathfrak p}$ is the localization by $C\setminus\mathfrak p$. For any such choice let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal of $D$, $E=A\otimes_C D$, $F=B\otimes_C D$, and $\sigma_D,\tau_D:E\to F$ the induced homomorphisms. The induced groupoid has finite locally free projections and invariant ring exactly $D$. The ring $E$ is semilocal (it has finitely many maximal ideals), $\mathfrak mE$ is contained in their intersection, and all its maximal points belong to one orbit. The source projection has the same degree $r\geq1$ at every point of $\operatorname{Spec}E$: this degree is the dimension of the fibre coordinate algebra over the residue field of that point. There exist $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in E$ such that $\tau_D(x_1),\ldots,\tau_D(x_r)$ is an $E$-basis of $F$ via $\sigma_D$, and $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ is a $D$-basis of $E$. In particular $E$ is finite free over $D$, and
$$\phi_D:E\otimes_D E\longrightarrow F,\qquad x\otimes y\longmapsto\sigma_D(x)\tau_D(y)$$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset C$ and write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Apply the flat local residue-extension lemma to the local ring $C_{\mathfrak p}$ and the infinite field extension $k(T)/k$. This gives a nonzero local ring $D$ with infinite residue field and a flat local map $C_{\mathfrak p}\to D$. The flat-local faithful-flatness lemma applies to every such choice, not just the constructed one, so each is faithfully flat.

For any chosen $D$, its flatness over $C_{\mathfrak p}$ implies its flatness over $C$ by the flat-over-localization equivalence, applied to $C\to C_{\mathfrak p}$. The sequence $0\to C\to A\xrightarrow{\sigma-\tau}B$ is exact by the definition of $C$. Flat tensor exactness gives $0\to D\to E\xrightarrow{\sigma_D-\tau_D}F$ exact. Thus $D\to E$ is injective and its image is exactly the invariant ring. In particular $E\ne0$.

The groupoid-base-change lemma supplies the induced groupoid on $\operatorname{Spec}E,\operatorname{Spec}F$ and its finite locally free projections. Apply integral invariants to this groupoid, using the identification of its invariant ring with $D$ from step 2: $E$ is integral over $D$. Apply orbit fibres to the same groupoid: $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is surjective and two points above the same prime of $D$ are joined by an arrow of $\operatorname{Spec}F$.

By maximal contraction for integral extensions, every maximal ideal of $E$ contracts to the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $D$, hence contains $\mathfrak mE$. Conversely, every prime above $\mathfrak m$ is maximal by the prime-over-maximal lemma. Surjectivity in step 3 gives one such maximal point $u$. Every maximal point $v$ is in the orbit of $u$, hence is the target of an arrow whose source is $u$. The source fibre is finite, because the source morphism is finite. Consequently there are finitely many maximal points of $E$, all in one orbit, and $\mathfrak mE$ is contained in their intersection.

Apply invariant rank strata to the base-changed affine groupoid. Its source degree is a positive integer and its rank strata are invariant open-and-closed subsets. Since all maximal points form one orbit, they lie in a single rank stratum, say the stratum of rank $r\ge1$. Every prime ideal of $E$ lies in a maximal ideal. An open-and-closed rank stratum containing that maximal point contains its generalizations, so every point belongs to the rank-$r$ stratum. This proves constant degree on all of $\operatorname{Spec}E$, with degree interpreted as fibre dimension exactly as in the cited statement.

source.place: Tag 03BI (lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free); Tag 03BM, third and final paragraphs.

proof.text: For the source $g:\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}E$, apply finite flat pushforward to the rank-one module $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$. Its pushforward is finite locally free. The affine-sections lemma implies that its global sections $P=F$, viewed as an $E$-module via $\sigma_D$, are finite projective. The standard-free-cover lemma gives a finite principal-open cover on which $P$ is finite free. At every point its rank equals the source fibre dimension, which is $r$ by step 5: reducing a free chart modulo the point identifies its basis with a basis of that fibre. Thus $P$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r$ in the module sense required by the semilocal basis lemma.

source.place: Tag 03BM, final paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat), affine module interpretation.

proof.text: Right exactness of tensor product preserves the surjectivity of $\phi$ after tensoring over $C$ with $D$. The resulting source $(A\otimes_C A)\otimes_C D$ identifies with $E\otimes_D E$ by $(a\otimes b)\otimes d\mapsto(a\otimes d)\otimes(b\otimes1)$; the inverse sends $(a\otimes d)\otimes(b\otimes d')$ to $(a\otimes b)\otimes dd'$. The balancing relations show these formulas are well-defined and inverse. Under them the map is $\phi_D$. Therefore every element of $F$ is a finite sum $\sum_j\sigma_D(y_j)\tau_D(z_j)$. Put $N=\tau_D(E)\subseteq P$. Since $\tau_D$ agrees with $\sigma_D$ on $D$, $N$ is a $D$-submodule, and the displayed expressions say its $E$-linear span is $P$.

source.place: Tag 03BM, final paragraph, surjective tensor comparison and its generating submodule.

proof.text: Apply the semilocal submodule basis lemma with local ring $D$, semilocal algebra $E$, module $P=F$ via $\sigma_D$, and submodule $N=\tau_D(E)$. Its hypotheses are respectively the chosen infinite residue field, the Jacobson-radical containment from step 4, constant rank $r\ge1$ from steps 5-6, and generation from step 7. Obtain a basis $n_1,\ldots,n_r\in N$ and choose $x_j\in E$ with $\tau_D(x_j)=n_j$. Apply groupoid basis descent to this same groupoid and its invariant ring $D$: $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ is a $D$-basis of $E$ and $\phi_D$ is an isomorphism. This proves finite freeness and all the asserted conclusions.

The item takes the module via sigma with submodule tau(E), matching 03C8 and lem-a1-affine-groupoid-basis-descent. Step 1 gets D from 03C3 with residue field k(T), which is infinite, and faithful flatness from 00HR for every choice. Step 2 uses the iff clause of flat-over-localization in the right direction; sigma-tau is C-linear because sigma and tau agree on C, and tensoring the equalizer with D shows the invariant ring is D and E is nonzero. Step 3 takes the base-changed groupoid from basechange-polynomial-norm. That node states the groupoid only over D, while integral-invariants and orbit-fibres need an absolute one. I checked this is elementary: an H-point makes H a D-scheme, and s_D, t_D are over D. Step 4: maximal ideals lie over m (00OI, 00GS) and are all t of the finite fibre of s over one maximal point u, so E is semilocal with mE in Jac(E). Step 5: the rank strata satisfy s^-1(U_r)=t^-1(U_r), so they are invariant; the single orbit of maximal points lies in one stratum, and open strata are closed under generalization, so the rank is a constant r>=1. Step 6: finite-flat pushforward, projective affine sections and 00NX give a principal-open free cover with fibre rank r; empty charts are trivially rank r, a case the step does not write out. Step 7: I checked the reassociation (A⊗A)⊗D to E⊗_D E; it shows tau_D(E) is a D-submodule whose E-span is F. Step 8 checks every hypothesis of semilocal-submodule-basis, then applies basis-descent with invariant ring D. Small cases checked: the identity groupoid (r=1), the swap action of Z/2 on k×k (r=2), and a trivial group action (excluded because phi is not surjective). No duplicate found among the 03BM or infinite-residue-field nodes; comparison-preparation, which assumes an equivalence relation, is rightly not cited.
